 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. In this story After a thrilling, competitive 2026 NWSL season , it all comes down to this. The Washington Spirit and the Kansas City Current will face off Saturday (8 p.m. ET, CBS) for what is sure to be a lively, star-studded NWSL championship.
 The Spirit advanced to their third straight final after dispatching the upstart Utah Royals, who had capped off a surprising season with a quarterfinals upset over the San Diego Wave. Meanwhile, the Current got revenge for last season's early playoff exit with a 2-1 victory over 2026 Shield winners Gotham FC.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The battle between No. 3 Washington and No. 4 Kansas City is set to be a good one. The teams split their two matchups this year, with the Spirit rolling to a 4-0 win in April and the Current snatching a 2-1 win last month.
 Both teams have dynamic forwards and dominant midfields, but it's the Spirit, by a bit of luck and a lot of grit, that have earned the home final at Washington's Audi Field. The Current, meanwhile, will try their best to spoil that home-field advantage while vying for their first NWSL title.
 Is the third time the charm for the Spirit?
 Though Washington is only five years removed from a championship, the Spirit have gotten tantalizingly close to another title over the past few years. In 2024, Washington returned to the championship match, but fell to the Orlando Pride 1-0 in a frustrating loss. Last year, the Spirit ended up back in the championship match, and again fell 1-0 as No. 8-seeded Gotham completed a Cinderella run .
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement It's been a frustrating run for a Spirit side stacked with some of the best players in the league, and one of the most cohesive products on the field. To lose those two finals is one thing, but to do so without scoring despite several opportunities is another. Washington intends to change that narrative; anything short of the trophy will be a major disappointment. But with a home-field advantage at Audi Field and players like Trinity Rodman playing at their peak, this might just be the year the Spirit break the cycle.
 Will the Current's depth get them the win?
 One year after a record-breaking NWSL Shield run , the Current got off to a slow start this season, but bounced back to secure the No. 4 seed. Kansas City has been overflowing with talent over the last several seasons, but has made it to the Final only once in franchise history, losing to the Portland Thorns in 2022.
 This season, Kansas City has experienced a surprising amount of change: Young star midfielder Claire Hutton was traded to Bay FC and replaced by another young star midfielder, Croix Bethune, while high-scoring veteran forward Bia Zaneratto left for Brazil in the offseason. Vlatko Andonovski was promoted out of the head coach position and replaced by Chris Armas before leaving the organization altogether .
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Still, the Current's depth has been keeping them afloat all season, with the team scoring a league-high 54 goals (tied with Angel City) throughout the year. Kansas City's squad is chock-full of potential scorers, with 12 different Current players getting on the score sheet this season. Haley Hopkins, who got the game-winner in Sunday's semifinal, leads the team with 13 goals, with two-time MVP Temwa Chawinga close behind with 12 goals; three others (Debinha, Michelle Cooper and Croix Bethune) also picked up more than five goals apiece. A win against Washington will need to come from the Current's ability to rely on several different players to score in the most important moments.
 Players to watch
 Trinity Rodman
 She's the face of the NWSL, an MVP nominee and the league's first two million-dollar player . And yet it's difficult to overrate Trinity Rodman: After dealing with injuries last year, the Spirit forward is having one of the best seasons of her career. Rodman leads Washington in every major offensive category, with 14 goals and 10 assists (tied for second in the league), and is also great on defense in a pinch.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement As further evidence of her importance to the team, Rodman played nearly every minute for the Spirit this season — very unusual for a forward, and even more so for someone with Rodman's injury history. But Rodman's ability to stay in high gear for a full 90 has been a major asset for Washington.
 The other reason to keep an eye on Rodman during this game? She wants that trophy — bad . The 24-year-old forward helped the Spirit to their first and only NWSL title during her Rookie of the Year season in 2021. Over the past two seasons, she's fallen short of the championship twice, but will try her hardest to make this year different.
 "This team right here, I would do anything for them," Rodman said on the broadcast after Washington's semifinal win.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Croix Bethune
 This one is personal for Bethune: The 25-year-old Current midfielder is competing in the NWSL Final again, but this time it's against her former team.
 After spending the first two years of her NWSL career with the Spirit, Bethune was traded from Washington to Kansas City in February as part of a blockbuster trade. The move was a surprise to fans — Bethune was a fan favorite in D.C. — but set the midfielder up to become a centerpiece of the reigning Shield winners.
 It took Bethune a few months to find her footing with Kansas City. But Bethune has been excellent all season: She won Midfielder of the Year for the second time in her career, fulfilling a preseason goal to repeat the honor after winning it for her stellar rookie season. Bethune leads the league in assists (with 11) and has created the most chances (45) of anyone on her team, per Fotmob. The midfielder's vision and playmaking has been clear in the playoffs. And during Sunday's semifinal, Bethune scored first with a beautiful, nearly physics-defying direct free-kick that ended up in the bottom corner of the goal.
 Expect Bethune to show some more of that talent on Saturday, especially given the stakes. A championship would be sweet, but doing it by beating her former team would be even sweeter.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Temwa Chawinga
 You can't talk about Kansas City's recent success without talking about Temwa Chawinga, a brilliant striker whose speed and penchant for goal-scoring have shaken up the league. Injuries kept the two-time MVP out for about a third of the season, but Chawinga still finished the year with 12 goals (sixth in the league) and picked up a nomination for 2026 NWSL MVP.
 In Sunday's win over Gotham, Chawinga played the full 90, indicating that she's at full fitness and ready to put pressure on the Spirit back line.
 Clara Luvanga
 It's early, but Washington appears to have struck gold with the acquisition of Clara Luvanga, who signed with the Spirit in September after three years with Saudi Arabia's Al-Nassr. Though a fresh face in the league, Luvanga has quickly proven to be a lethal threat for Washington: In just seven matches (four starts), the Tanzanian forward has picked up four goals and three assists.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Two of those goals have been game-winners — including in Saturday's semifinal, when Luvanga took advantage of a defensive mistake to seal the Spirit's trip to the final.
 With the striker's early results in mind, Luvanga seems poised for another big moment in Saturday's matchup.
